audience.description: Broker target that releases the person's GitHub grant (`tokenExchangeBroker.targets.<audience>.grantIssuer`).

clientID.description: This server's client id at muster's token-exchange broker (`tokenExchangeBroker.brokerClients.<id>`, allowed audience `github`).

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret with the broker client credentials under `client-secret` (and optionally `client-id`) — the same Secret muster's `brokerClients.<id>.clientCredentialsSecretRef` reads. Empty leaves the broker client off.
Existing Secret with the CircleCI API token (read scope) under `token`, passed as `CIRCLECI_API_TOKEN`. Empty leaves it unset.

fullnameOverride.description: Override the fully qualified app name.

apiURL.description: GitHub API base URL; empty is api.github.com.

appID.description: The App used for unattended, read-only inventory reads (the giantswarm-align-files App) and its installation on the org. 0 leaves the App identity off.

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret with the App's PEM private key under `private-key`.

global.description: Platform-wide values an umbrella chart shares with every component and Helm forwards here. `oauth.*` reads the identity contract as its defaults: `global.identity.issuerUrl`, `global.identity.clientId`, `global.identity.existingSecret`, `global.identity.ca.secretName` / `.key`, and `global.domain` for the OAuth base URL. Empty here; a standalone install sets `oauth.*` directly.

tag.description: Image tag. Defaults to the chart appVersion.

connectTimeout.description: How long the server waits for the store at start (a Go duration), retrying with backoff, before it gives up and exits; it serves meanwhile, liveness passing and readiness failing until the store answers, so a Valkey that starts after the manager — a volume binding late, a restart — costs no container restart within the window. `"0"` waits for ever.

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret with the bearer token of the internal endpoints under `token`: `POST /internal/refresh` (the reconciler workflow's trigger after a run, with the run as `lastRun`) and `/internal/sweep`. Empty disables them (404).

org.description: The GitHub organization the inventory covers.

staleDays.description: Stale period of the orphan score in days (no commit by a person, no Renovate activity within it).

concurrency.description: Parallel CircleCI and engine reads during a sweep.

engineChecks.description: Run the engine's set-up checks in read mode for every accepted declaration during a sweep (REST as the App, about ten calls per repository). A `refresh_repository` always runs them.

graphqlBudgetFloor.description: Stop a sweep cleanly when the GraphQL budget's remaining points fall below this; 0 never stops.

interval.description: Full sweep over the org every interval (a Go duration); `"0"` turns the schedule off. The first sweep runs at start when the last one is older than the interval.

valkeyAddress.description: Address (`host:port`) of the Valkey the inventory lives in, passed to the server as `VALKEY_ADDR`. Empty derives the subchart's Service, `<valkey.valkey.fullnameOverride>.<namespace>.svc:6379`; required when `valkey.enabled` is false.

auth.description: How muster authenticates to this server; rendered only with `oauth.enabled`. `forwardToken` makes muster forward the session's Dex id_token byte-identical. `requiredAudiences` are extra audiences that token must carry (the Dex cross-client audience of the platform, e.g. `dex-k8s-authenticator`); they are trusted as bearer audiences by construction.

autoStart.description: Start the server connection when muster initializes.

enabled.description: Register this server with muster by rendering an `mcpservers.muster.giantswarm.io` CR in the release namespace. Tools then appear as `x_<name>_<tool>`.

labels.description: Extra labels on the MCPServer CR.

name.description: MCPServer CR name (drives the tool prefix).

url.description: muster's base URL as reached from the pod (for example `http://muster.muster.svc:8090`): the broker exchange goes to `<url>/oauth/token`. Empty leaves the broker client off; `get_info` reports it.

allowPublicClientRegistration.description: Accept unauthenticated dynamic client registration (labs only).

baseURL.description: Public base URL of this server: the issuer of its own OAuth metadata (https, or http on loopback). Empty derives `https://<fullname>.<global.domain>` when `global.domain` is set.

allowPrivateURLs.description: Let the issuer resolve to a private or loopback address (an in-cluster Dex).

caSecret.description: Secret with the CA of a Dex that serves a private certificate; mounted and passed as `DEX_CA_FILE`. Empty name falls back to `global.identity.ca.secretName` / `global.identity.ca.key`.

clientID.description: Dex OAuth client ID this server is registered as. Empty falls back to `global.identity.clientId`.

issuerURL.description: Dex issuer URL. Empty falls back to `global.identity.issuerUrl`.

enabled.description: Make the server an OAuth 2.1 resource server (mcp-oauth): the MCP endpoint requires a bearer token the platform Dex issued, and every call carries the caller's identity and id_token — the subject token of the broker exchange that releases the caller's GitHub grant. muster forwards the session's id_token byte-identical (MCPServer `auth.forwardToken`, rendered below); it is validated against Dex's JWKS when its audience is in `trustedAudiences`. Off: anonymous — no caller, no grant, tools report so; only for a server nothing but a trusted proxy can reach.

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret with the Dex client secret under `dex-client-secret`. Empty falls back to `global.identity.existingSecret`; without that, the chart renders a Secret from `oauth.dex.clientSecret`.

allowPrivateIPs.description: Let the IdP's JWKS endpoint resolve to a private address when validating forwarded tokens (an in-cluster Dex).

trustedAudiences.description: OAuth client IDs whose Dex id_tokens are accepted as bearer tokens (SSO token forwarding). Empty falls back to `[global.identity.clientId]`. The server trusts the union of this list and `muster.mcpServer.auth.requiredAudiences`.

replicaCount.description: Number of replicas. The server holds its state in Valkey; more than one is fine.

audience.description: The audience of the projected token — the gateway's `reviews.audience`; this ServiceAccount must be in its `reviews.allowedCallers`.

channels.description: Slack channel IDs by the channel name a team's policy file carries (`slackChannel`): the gateway takes IDs. A policy file that carries the ID itself needs no entry.

gatewayURL.description: klaus-gateway's base URL as reached from the pod (for example `http://klaus-gateway.agent-platform.svc:8080`): lifecycle and transfer asks go to `POST /reviews`, notices and completion messages to `POST /notices`, authenticated with this pod's projected ServiceAccount token for `audience`. Empty leaves the asks undelivered; the tools say so and approving on GitHub stays equivalent.

ref.description: The branch the files are read from and pull requests target.

repository.description: The repository that holds the team files (`repositories/<team>.yaml`, the desired state) and the policy files (`repository-setup/<team>.yaml`); every write is a pull request against it, opened as the caller.

valkey.description: The inventory store: the Giant Swarm `valkey` app as a subchart (its values live under `valkey.valkey`, the upstream chart's). One replica on an RWO volume with `Recreate`, so a rollout does not deadlock on the volume; the store is a cache — every record is rebuilt from the team files and GitHub — so the restart gap costs nothing. Set `valkey.enabled: false` and `inventory.valkeyAddress` to use a Valkey outside the release.
